content.text: Allowing clients to point to existing repository resources as ACLs poses some security challenges that need to be considered.
If somebody points to a resource already controlled by an ACL.  Who wins - that resource's ACL, or acl:Control statements in the resource itself?
Are there resources that, by the permissions granted to them, cannot be specified as the target of an ACL link?  For example, what happens if I specify an ACL that I don't have permission to read?
I would suggest the following constraints:
ACLs can not have ACLs (with the exception of the default/root ACL)
If a client does not have read-access to a resource, then that client should not be able to reference that resource as an ACL

:  According to the SOLID/WAC spec (referenced above in the description), acl:Control gives the ability to view and modify an ACL resource.   So I would strike constraint 2 since it is conceivable that a user might not have read or write access to a resource, but still be able to control the ACL.
Pending response to code review comments.
The acl:Control mode indicates the user/role who has permission to modify an ACL.  As it is part of the SOLID WAC spec, it needs to be implemented.

According to the SOLID/WAC: acl:Control is a special-case access mode that gives an agent the ability to view and modify the ACL of a resource. Note that it doesn't automatically imply that the agent has acl:Read or acl:Write access to the resource itself, just to its corresponding ACL document. For example, a resource owner may disable their own Write access (to prevent accidental over-writing of a resource by an app), but be able to change their access levels at a later point (since they retain acl:Control access).
Thus for this ticket to be consider complete the following must be true:
1.  In order to view, create or modify an ACL Resource (ACL A)  of a given Resource (Resource B) , the client must have acl:Control permission on Resource B.
2. If the previous test fails, a 403 (Forbidden) code should be returned.

I would suggest the following constraints:

  2. If a client does not have read-access to a resource, then that client should not be able to reference that resource as an ACL
